/**
 * Single source of truth for the OAuthProvider config.
 *
 * `index.ts` constructs the live provider; admin tooling (e.g. the
 * OAuth-clients viewer) constructs a read-only `OAuthHelpers` instance
 * via `getOAuthApi(opts, env)` and MUST use the identical KV+path
 * config so the helpers point at the same data the live provider
 * wrote. Extracted here so we can't drift.
 *
 * The `defaultHandler` is plumbed through as a parameter because
 * helpers paths (listClients, lookupClient, etc.) never invoke it —
 * admin code can pass a stub, while `index.ts` passes the real Hono
 * app.
 */

import type { ExportedHandler } from '@cloudflare/workers-types'
import type {
  OAuthProviderOptions,
  TokenExchangeCallbackOptions
} from '@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider'
import { McpSessionDO } from '../mcp/session-do'
import type { Env } from '../env'
import { mcpResourceUrl } from '../util/mcp-host'
import { stampTokenExchange } from './login-activity'

const NOOP_HANDLER: ExportedHandler<Env> = {
  fetch: () => new Response('not used by admin helpers', { status: 500 })
}

/**
 * Access-token lifetime: 7 days, not the library's 1 h default.
 *
 * Claude's hosted connector (Desktop / claude.ai) does not refresh when an
 * expired access token gets a 401 on /mcp — it shows the user a "Reconnect"
 * prompt, and that click is what runs the (succeeding) refresh_token grant.
 * With 1 h tokens every idle gap longer than an hour cost a prompt (2026-11
 * field finding: 401 bursts on /mcp, each followed only by a refresh after
 * the user acted, never a server-side rejection). A longer token makes the
 * prompt roughly weekly at worst.
 *
 * Why this is safe here: access tokens live in KV, so suspend/delete
 * (`revokeAllUserGrants`) still kills them instantly, and the session DO
 * re-checks user status on init. The cost is a longer useful life for a
 * leaked bearer. Must stay well below `MCP_LOGIN_IDLE_DAYS` so an active
 * client always refreshes inside the idle window.
 */
export const MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60

/**
 * A login lasts as long as it keeps refreshing (see oauth/login-activity.ts).
 *
 * Both TTLs below are passed as `undefined` on purpose — the library then
 * writes the grant and the DCR client record to KV with NO expiration, and
 * expiry becomes ours to decide. That is the only way to get a sliding
 * session out of this library: `refreshTokenTTL` is stamped once, at the
 * authorization-code exchange, and the refresh path re-saves the same
 * absolute instant (it even refuses a `refreshTokenTTL` returned from the
 * token-exchange callback). `clientRegistrationTTL` behaves the same way
 * from the registration moment, so leaving it at its 90 d default would cap
 * the login independently — the final refresh would just fail
 * `invalid_client` instead of `invalid_grant`.
 *
 * What replaces them: `tokenExchangeCallback` stamps every exchange into
 * `oauth_grant_activity`, and the nightly `grant-idle-prune` job revokes
 * grants that have been silent for `MCP_LOGIN_IDLE_DAYS`. Instant lockout is
 * unaffected — suspend/delete still calls `revokeAllUserGrants`, and the
 * session DO re-checks user status on init.
 *
 * `env` is required: the canonical resource (below) is derived from it, and
 * admin tooling building `OAuthHelpers` from these same options (see the
 * module header) must name the identical resource. Those helpers never
 * exchange a token, so the callback being installed there is inert.
 *
 * Resource (workers-oauth-provider 1.x): every grant and access token is
 * bound to exactly one resource, compared exactly — see `mcpResourceUrl`.
 * Only `/mcp` is served. The legacy HTTP+SSE endpoint (`/sse`) was dropped
 * at the 1.x upgrade: 1.x cannot cover two sibling paths with one resource,
 * the SSE transport is deprecated in MCP, and no stored grant was bound to
 * it (2026-11 KV scan of the largest deployment: 0 of 444).
 */
export function oauthProviderOptions(
  env: Env,
  defaultHandler: ExportedHandler<Env> = NOOP_HANDLER
): OAuthProviderOptions<Env> {
  // apiHandlers requires ExportedHandlerWithFetch (Required fetch);
  // our handler carries `fetch` at the value level but its declared
  // type doesn't line up exactly, so the map is cast once.
  const apiHandlers = {
    '/mcp': McpSessionDO.serve('/mcp', { binding: 'MCP_SESSION_DO' })
  } as OAuthProviderOptions<Env>['apiHandlers']
  return {
    apiHandlers,
    defaultHandler,
    resourceMetadata: { resource: mcpResourceUrl(env) },
    authorizeEndpoint: '/oauth/authorize',
    tokenEndpoint: '/oauth/token',
    clientRegistrationEndpoint: '/oauth/register',
    // Explicit `undefined` — it overrides the library defaults (30 d / 90 d)
    // through the options spread, and is what makes the KV records
    // expiration-less. See the note above before "simplifying" these away.
    refreshTokenTTL: undefined,
    clientRegistrationTTL: undefined,
    accessTokenTTL: MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
    tokenExchangeCallback: (opts: TokenExchangeCallbackOptions) => stampTokenExchange(env, opts),
    scopesSupported: ['mcp']
  }
}

Internal company server.

Several users have to reconnect our custom connector again and again. Scheduled tasks fail because the tools are not available.

06:04:29.295  POST /api/auth/oauth2/token   400  invalid_grant
06:04:29.313  POST /api/auth/oauth2/token   200

The timeline points at three separate failures, not one, and separating them makes the recovery path server-side only:

1. Two live sessions for one subject. `initialize` at 19:49:08 opened session B while A was still active on the same OAuth family. 2. DCR is not reused, and that is why reconnect does not restore tools into open conversations. Eight client_ids since Oct 15 means each Allow click minted a new registration. My suggestion, and the most useful change here: on `POST /register`, hash the client metadata you actually key on (redirect_uris, token_endpoint_auth_method, grant_types, software_id, client_name) and return the existing registration for an identical tuple inside a subject session instead of minting a new one. RFC 7591 section 3.2.1 permits the authorization server to return an existing client for duplicate metadata. That turns reconnect from "new identity" into "refresh the same identity", which is the only version of reconnect that can re-attach an open conversation.

3. 80 `tools/list` calls in an hour with 89 tools is the third. Re-attach is cheap for you and expensive for the client, and large inventories have a second failure mode that looks exactly like this: clients that cap the list (count or payload bytes) drop tools silently and then report "the tool does not exist". Worth measuring whether the missing tools are always the ones late in your ordering.

On your question about `notifications/tools/list_changed`: it cannot cover the case you hit. The notification travels on a live session stream, and you have a 1006 bridge close plus `GET` returning 405, so there is no stream to deliver on when the loss happens. It does help the narrower case where the session survives and the inventory changes, so keep it, but do not expect it to recover an open conversation.

Two things that do work without a client release: keep one active session per (client_id, subject) by returning the same `Mcp-Session-Id` on an `initialize` that arrives with an Authorization header for a family that already has a live session, and add a short grace window before answering 404 for a session id minted recently, answering with a rotated `Mcp-Session-Id` header instead. We build a multi-connector MCP server (corpusiq.io) and hit the same shape: a client re-listing on re-attach while the conversation keeps its earlier snapshot is indistinguishable from a server that dropped the tools. The only levers the server owns are identity stability and list cost.

The chain rules out every refresh-related workaround: since Nov 9 the connector has never refreshed once, yet it re-registered and forced a full sign-in seven times.

## What the rows say

- **Since the 7-day tokens went live (Nov 8 evening):** every login has `created` equal to `last refresh`. The connector held an access token valid for a week, never needed the token endpoint, and still came back with a new client id on Nov 9, 10, 11 (three times), 12 and 14.
- **Before November:** logins lasted days to weeks (Oct 12 → Oct 29, Sep 29 → Oct 10). From Nov 3 they shrink to two days, then one, then less.
- **Claude Code control** (`JizYCK`): one login since Oct 12, still healthy.

(The script's date filter was off by a year, which is why you see rows back to September; it didn't affect the reading.)

## What that does to the workaround list

| Workaround | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Rotation replay for concurrent refreshes (#1194) | Ruled out: no refresh happens at all. |
| Root-path aliases for the fallback (#1169) | Not the trigger here, since the fallback starts from a failed refresh. Still cheap insurance. |
| Longer access tokens | Already done; the chain shows it didn't help. |
| CIMD | The only lever left. The connector throws away its client registration and tokens together; with CIMD there is no registration to lose. |

The Nov 3 onset lines up with other reports in the tracker dated Nov 2–4 (#1224, #1214, one commenter says "since about 2026-11-02"). That points to a change on Anthropic's side rather than anything we shipped; our last deploy before that was Oct 12.

## Recommendation

Build CIMD support plus the aliases and release it for a test. It is a bet, not a proven fix: if the connector also discards its tokens under a stable client id, the morning sign-in stays. The evidence for it is that Claude picks CIMD over dynamic registration when offered (#1194) and one operator reports CIMD sign-ins holding where the registered ones did not.

If CIMD doesn't stop it, the fallback is to use the local `ctxlayer` entry on your machine (the Claude Code path, which has held one login since Oct 12) rather than the hosted connector.

CIMD support and the root-path aliases are built, and `bun run verify` passes (731 unit, 55 web, 537 integration). Nothing is committed or deployed.

## What changed

- **CIMD on:** the provider now accepts a client's published metadata URL as its `client_id` and advertises that in the discovery document. Dynamic registration stays available. It had never been enabled before, despite the compat flag being set.
- **Sign-in keeps earlier logins for CIMD clients:** a CIMD client id is shared by Desktop, web and mobile, so the library default of revoking the user's previous grant would sign the other surfaces out. That revoke is now skipped for CIMD clients only; the nightly idle sweep still retires unused ones.
- **Root-path aliases:** `/token`, `/register` and `/authorize` now behave exactly like `/oauth/token`, `/oauth/register` and `/oauth/authorize`.
- **Asset routing:** those three paths are added to `run_worker_first` in `wrangler.toml` and in `../ctxlayer-ops/wrangler.template.toml`. The second is in the ops repo, which I edited because yukitools renders its config from it; without it the aliases would not take effect there.
- **Admin clients viewer:** CIMD logins have no stored client record, so the viewer now adds a row for each CIMD client that holds a login. This part has no test.

The new tests cover the aliases (register, code exchange, refresh via the root paths) and a full CIMD sign-in and refresh with nothing written to the client store.

## What is not known yet

- **Whether your existing connector switches to CIMD on its own.** One report shows an explicit "Use Claude's published identity (CIMD)" option in the add-connector dialog, so you may have to remove and re-add the connector after the release.
- **Whether a stable client id stops the connector discarding its tokens.** That only shows after a release.

## After you release

1. `https://mcp.yukitools.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` should show `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true`.
2. `POST https://mcp.yukitools.dev/token` should no longer return 405.
3. Sign in once more, then rerun the login-chain script. The script prints only the first six characters of the client id, so a CIMD login shows as `https:`. If the morning prompts then stop, the bet paid off.

The main files are [provider-config.ts](apps/worker/src/oauth/provider-config.ts), [default-endpoints.ts](apps/worker/src/oauth/default-endpoints.ts), [cimd.ts](apps/worker/src/oauth/cimd.ts) and [complete-mcp.ts](apps/worker/src/idp/complete-mcp.ts).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Roll the app repo's CURRENT checkout out to ctxlayer deployments
# (scenario B). Re-renders each per-host config from the template + registry
# (so it works on a fresh app checkout), then migrate THEN deploy.
#
# This is the ONLY upgrade path — nothing auto-upgrades. Each host keeps
# running whatever commit it was last released with (visible in the SPA
# footer / GET /api/health), so upgrades are deliberate and stageable.
#
# Usage:
#   [APP_REPO=/path/to/ctxlayer] scripts/release-all.sh                 # all hosts in tenants.json
#   scripts/release-all.sh dev stage          # only these hosts
#   scripts/release-all.sh --migrate-only     # apply migrations, skip deploy
set -euo pipefail

OPS_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
APP_REPO="${APP_REPO:-$(cd "$OPS_ROOT/../ctxlayer" 2>/dev/null && pwd || true)}"
[[ -n "$APP_REPO" && -f "$APP_REPO/wrangler.toml" ]] || {
  echo "✗ APP_REPO not found (sibling ../ctxlayer). Set APP_REPO=/path/to/ctxlayer." >&2
  exit 1
}
TEMPLATE="$OPS_ROOT/wrangler.template.toml"
REGISTRY="$OPS_ROOT/tenants.json"
[ -s "$REGISTRY" ] || { echo "✗ no tenant registry at $REGISTRY." >&2; exit 1; }

# Preflight: fail fast on deploy-scheme naming drift (binding/cron parity) so a
# templated tenant can't silently lose a binding or a queue/cron consumer.
APP_REPO="$APP_REPO" "$OPS_ROOT/scripts/check-deploy-scheme.sh"

MIGRATE_ONLY=0
SELECTED=()
for a in "$@"; do
  if [[ "$a" == "--migrate-only" ]]; then MIGRATE_ONLY=1; else SELECTED+=("$a"); fi
done
if [[ ${#SELECTED[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  # No `mapfile`/`readarray` — macOS ships bash 3.2, where they don't exist.
  while IFS= read -r slug; do SELECTED+=("$slug"); done < <(jq -r 'keys[]' "$REGISTRY")
fi
[[ ${#SELECTED[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo "✗ nothing to release." >&2; exit 1; }

# Cross-account guard (see docs/yukitools-provisioning.md): keep only the
# selected hosts that live in the ACTIVE Cloudflare account. The active account
# is CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID when a per-account token is exported, else the satisa
# OAuth login wrangler defaults to. A tenant's account is its registry `account`
# (entries without one predate multi-account and live in satisa). The accounts
# use different tokens that AREN'T in the registry, so deploying a tenant against
# the wrong login would create resources in the wrong account (or fail) —
# mismatched hosts are skipped here, BEFORE the build, so a wrong-creds run fails
# fast. Run release-all.sh once per account with that account's creds exported.
SATISA_ACCOUNT="${SATISA_ACCOUNT:-a65126d6fa58bfd6da28c3504b0aa859}"
ACTIVE_ACCOUNT="${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID:-$SATISA_ACCOUNT}"
DEPLOYABLE=()
for SLUG in "${SELECTED[@]}"; do
  TENANT_ACCOUNT=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].account // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  TENANT_ACCOUNT="${TENANT_ACCOUNT:-$SATISA_ACCOUNT}"
  if [[ "$TENANT_ACCOUNT" != "$ACTIVE_ACCOUNT" ]]; then
    echo "⏭ $SLUG: in account $TENANT_ACCOUNT ≠ active $ACTIVE_ACCOUNT — skipping (export that account's creds to deploy it)." >&2
    continue
  fi
  DEPLOYABLE+=("$SLUG")
